original_question: Is there a finitely generated, residually finite Π-group that is not effectively residually finite?
target_in_paper: Section 6 (Andre Nies), under “Profinite groups,” specifically Problem 15(b): “Is there a f.g., residually finite Π-group that is not effectively r.f.?” ([tianyuan.amss.ac.cn](https://tianyuan.amss.ac.cn/upload/fab78d36-bd52-42eb-84d3-ff99c953bb08/20250708/67111751937959724.pdf?utm_source=openai))
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper’s official formulation: it has the correct existential quantifier, the finitely generated hypothesis, the residually finite hypothesis, the Π-group hypothesis, and the negation of effective residual finiteness. In substance, it is essentially Problem 15(b) verbatim. ([tianyuan.amss.ac.cn](https://tianyuan.amss.ac.cn/upload/fab78d36-bd52-42eb-84d3-ff99c953bb08/20250708/67111751937959724.pdf?utm_source=openai))
missing_details: The paper’s “Π-group” is not stand-alone in your draft: nearby Theorem 14 defines this as a finitely generated group whose word problem is Π^0_1. ([tianyuan.amss.ac.cn](https://tianyuan.amss.ac.cn/upload/fab78d36-bd52-42eb-84d3-ff99c953bb08/20250708/67111751937959724.pdf?utm_source=openai))

The paper gives a specific formal meaning of “effectively residually finite” just before Theorem 14: for a finitely generated group presented as S = F_k/N, there must be an algorithm which, on input w ∈ F_k, in the case w ∉ N, computes a finite group Q and a homomorphism r : F_k → Q such that r(N) = {e} and r(w) ≠ e. ([tianyuan.amss.ac.cn](https://tianyuan.amss.ac.cn/upload/fab78d36-bd52-42eb-84d3-ff99c953bb08/20250708/67111751937959724.pdf?utm_source=openai))

To make the question fully self-contained, you should spell out that “residually finite” means every nonidentity element survives in some finite quotient; the paper states the problem in abbreviated form and does not re-expand this standard term in Problem 15(b). ([tianyuan.amss.ac.cn](https://tianyuan.amss.ac.cn/upload/fab78d36-bd52-42eb-84d3-ff99c953bb08/20250708/67111751937959724.pdf?utm_source=openai))

To avoid ambiguity, the draft should make clear that “Π-group” here is computability-theoretic shorthand tied to Π^0_1 word problem, not the unrelated finite-group-theoretic notion of a π-group. ([tianyuan.amss.ac.cn](https://tianyuan.amss.ac.cn/upload/fab78d36-bd52-42eb-84d3-ff99c953bb08/20250708/67111751937959724.pdf?utm_source=openai))

If you want the question to be fully paper-faithful, it is helpful to retain the free-group/presentation notation S = F_k/N used in the nearby definition of effective residual finiteness, since that is how the input/output requirement is formalized. ([tianyuan.amss.ac.cn](https://tianyuan.amss.ac.cn/upload/fab78d36-bd52-42eb-84d3-ff99c953bb08/20250708/67111751937959724.pdf?utm_source=openai))
refined_question: Does there exist a finitely generated group S = F_k/N such that: (i) its word problem N ⊆ F_k is Π^0_1 (equivalently, S is a Π-group in the sense of the paper); (ii) S is residually finite, i.e. every nonidentity element of S survives in some finite quotient; but (iii) S is not effectively residually finite, meaning that there is no algorithm which, given w ∈ F_k with w ∉ N, outputs a finite group Q and a homomorphism r : F_k → Q such that r(N) = {e} and r(w) ≠ e? ([tianyuan.amss.ac.cn](https://tianyuan.amss.ac.cn/upload/fab78d36-bd52-42eb-84d3-ff99c953bb08/20250708/67111751937959724.pdf?utm_source=openai))
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, by Theorem 14, does there exist a finitely generated, residually finite group with Π^0_1 word problem that is not isomorphic to a subgroup of any computable profinite group generated by finitely many computable paths? ([tianyuan.amss.ac.cn](https://tianyuan.amss.ac.cn/upload/fab78d36-bd52-42eb-84d3-ff99c953bb08/20250708/67111751937959724.pdf?utm_source=openai))
justification: This paper is an open-problems list, so the nearest official target is not a conjecture but Problem 15(b) in Section 6. Your draft matches that target almost exactly. The only substantive incompleteness is that the paper relies on nearby context for the meanings of “Π-group” and “effectively residually finite”: Theorem 14 identifies a Π-group as a finitely generated group with Π^0_1 word problem, and the sentence immediately preceding Theorem 14 gives the precise algorithmic definition of effective residual finiteness using a presentation S = F_k/N. The alternate formulation follows directly from Theorem 14’s iff characterization. ([tianyuan.amss.ac.cn](https://tianyuan.amss.ac.cn/upload/fab78d36-bd52-42eb-84d3-ff99c953bb08/20250708/67111751937959724.pdf?utm_source=openai))
